title: FIPS provider enforcement: prevent silent load-order bypass
description:
The 'first-registered wins' dispatch rule means loading crypto2dev_kcapi.ko before crypto2dev_wolfssl.ko causes all algorithms to be served by the non-FIPS-gated kcapi provider. An application that intends to use FIPS-validated crypto gets silently un-gated crypto with no error, no warning, and no way to detect it without examining /proc or checking provider names via GET_STATE.

This is a security failure for the core use case: FIPS-validated userspace crypto.

Concrete scenario:
  insmod crypto2dev_kcapi.ko    # registers cbc(aes), gcm(aes), sha256, ...
  insmod crypto2dev_wolfssl.ko  # registers same algos — but kcapi already owns them
  # wolfssl is loaded, FIPS-operational, but never called

HUMAN DECISION NEEDED:

How should the API prevent this? Options:

A. Provider priority: FIPS-gated providers always win over non-FIPS providers for any algorithm both handle, regardless of registration order. Non-FIPS providers fill only algorithms the FIPS provider does not cover.
   Pro: Automatic safety, no API changes.
   Con: Makes load order semantics complex; two FIPS providers could still have ordering issues.

B. Per-fd FIPS enforcement: new ioctl CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_REQUIRE_FIPS that causes INIT to fail with -ENOENT if no FIPS-gated provider handles the requested algorithm, even if a non-FIPS provider does.
   Pro: Explicit, per-fd control.
   Con: Another ioctl; callers who do not call it get the current unsafe default.

C. Module parameter: crypto2dev_wolfssl.ko takes a module parameter 'priority=high' that causes it to re-register algorithms it handles, bumping kcapi out.
   Pro: Sysadmin-controlled without API change.
   Con: Not portable, fragile, does not help if wolfssl is not loaded at all.

D. Document and warn only: log pr_warn when a FIPS provider registers an algorithm already claimed by a non-FIPS provider. Make it the operator's responsibility.
   Pro: No API change.
   Con: Silent in production; operators will miss it.

Recommendation: A + B together. Priority ensures correct default; per-fd require-FIPS makes it auditable.

Work items once decision is made:
- Implement chosen enforcement mechanism in crypto2dev_registry.c
- Update crypto2dev_ioctl.h if per-fd ioctl chosen
- Add syslog warning on load-order FIPS bypass regardless of which option chosen
- Test: load kcapi first, verify FIPS-required fd gets -ENOENT for kcapi-only algo
